title: Baa, Baa, Black Sheep
lyrics: Baa, baa, black sheep,
Have you any wool?
Yes, sir, yes, sir,
Three bags full;
One for the master,
And one for the dame,
And one for the little boy
Who lives down the lane.

lyricsNote: Wikipedia「Modern version」节明确标注并说明该版由《The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes》给出，逐行照录，保留原标点。页面说明此谣为单节 trochaic metre，且两百五十年间文字几无变化。未凭记忆补写或改写。

title: Jack and Jill
lyrics: Jack and Jill went up the hill,
To fetch a pail of water;
Jack fell down, and broke, his crown,
And Jill came tumbling after.
Then up Jack got and off did trot,
As fast as he could caper,
To old Dame Dob, who patched his nob
With vinegar and brown paper.

title: Little Bo-Peep
lyrics: Little Bo-Peep has lost her sheep
And doesn't know where to find them.
Leave them alone and they'll come home,
Bringing their tails behind them.
Little Bo-peep fell fast asleep,
And dreamt she heard them bleating;
But when she awoke, she found it a joke,
For they were still all fleeting.
Then up she took her little crook,
Determined for to find them;
She found them indeed, but it made her heart bleed,
For they'd left their tails behind them.
It happened one day, as Bo-Peep did stray
Into a meadow hard by,
There she espied their tails side by side,
All hung on a tree to dry.
She heaved a sigh, and wiped her eye,
And over the hillocks went rambling,
And tried what she could, as a shepherdess should,
To tack each again to its lambkin.

title: Pat-a-Cake
lyrics: Pat-a-cake, pat-a-cake, baker's man.
Bake me a cake as fast as you can
Pat it, and roll it, and mark it with a B
And put it in the oven for Baby and me.

Down came the rain
And washed the spider out.
Out came the sun
And dried up all the rain
And the itsy bitsy spider climbed up the spout again.

London Bridge is falling down,
My fair lady.
Build it up with Iron Bars,
Iron Bars, Iron Bars,
Build it up with Iron Bars,
My fair lady.
Iron Bars will bend and break,
Bend and break, bend and break,
Iron bars will bend and break,
My fair lady.

He played knick-knack on my thumb (or drum).
With a knick-knack paddywhack,
Give a dog a bone.

title: Froggie Went a-Courtin'
lyrics: A frog he would a-wooing go,
Heigho, says Rowley,
Whether his mother would let him or no.
With a rowley powley, gammon and spinach,
Heigho, says Anthony Rowley!
So off he set with his opera hat,
Heigho, says Rowley,
And on the road he met with a rat.
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mr. Rat, will you go with me,
Heigho, says Rowley,
Kind Mistress Mousey for to see?'
With a rowley powley, etc.
And when they came to Mousey's hall,
Heigho, says Rowley,
They gave a loud knock, and they gave a loud call.
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mistress Mouse, are you within?'
Heigho, says Rowley.
'Oh yes, kind sirs, I'm sitting to spin.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mistress Mouse, will you give us some beer?
Heigho, says Rowley,
For Froggy and I are fond of good cheer.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mr. Frog, will you give us a song?
Heigho, says Rowley,
But let it be something that's not very long.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Indeed, Mistress Mouse,' replied Mr. Frog,
Heigho, says Rowley,
'A cold has made me as hoarse as a dog.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Since you have caught cold, Mr. Frog,' Mousey said,
Heigho, says Rowley,
'I'll sing you a song that I have just made.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
But while they were all a merry-making,
Heigho, says Rowley,
A cat and her kittens came tumbling in.
With a rowley powley, etc.
The cat she seized the rat by the crown;
Heigho, says Rowley,
The kittens they pulled the little mouse down.
With a rowley powley, etc.
This put Mr. Frog in a terrible fright;
Heigho, says Rowley,
He took up his hat, and wished them goodnight.
With a rowley powley, etc.
But as Froggy was crossing over a brook,
Heigho, says Rowley,
A lily-white duck came and gobbled him up,
With a rowley powley, etc.
So there was an end of one, two, and three,
Heigho, says Rowley,
The rat, and the mouse, and the little froggee,
With a rowley powley, gammon and spinach,
Heigho, says Anthony Rowley!

title: Yankee Doodle
lyrics: Yankee Doodle went to town
A-riding on a pony,
Stuck a feather in his cap
And called it macaroni.
[*Chorus*]
Yankee Doodle, keep it up,
Yankee Doodle dandy,
Mind the music and the step,
And with the girls be handy.
Father and I went down to camp,
Along with Captain Gooding,
And there we saw the men and boys
As thick as hasty pudding.
[*Chorus*]
And there we saw a thousand men
As rich as Squire David,
And what they wasted every day,
I wish it could be savèd.
[*Chorus*]
The 'lasses they eat every day,
Would keep a house a winter;
They have so much, that I'll be bound,
They eat it when they've a mind to.
[*Chorus*]
And there I see a swamping gun
Large as a log of maple,
Upon a deuced little cart,
A load for father's cattle.
[*Chorus*]
And every time they shoot it off,
It takes a horn of powder,
And makes a noise like father's gun,
Only a nation louder.
[*Chorus*]
I went as nigh to one myself
As 'Siah's underpinning;
And father went as nigh again,
I thought the deuce was in him.
[*Chorus*]
Cousin Simon grew so bold,
I thought he would have cocked it;
It scared me so I shrinked it off
And hung by father's pocket.
[*Chorus*]
And Cap'n Davis had a gun,
He kind of clapt his hand on't
And stuck a crooked stabbing iron
Upon the little end on't
[*Chorus*]
And there I see a pumpkin shell
As big as mother's basin,
And every time they touched it off
They scampered like the nation.
[*Chorus*]
I see a little barrel too,
The heads were made of leather;
They knocked on it with little clubs
And called the folks together.
[*Chorus*]
And there was Cap'n Washington,
And gentle folks about him;
They say he's grown so 'tarnal proud
He will not ride without 'em.
[*Chorus*]
He got him on his meeting clothes,
Upon a slapping stallion;
He sat the world along in rows,
In hundreds and in millions.
[*Chorus*]
The flaming ribbons in his hat,
They looked so tearing fine, ah,
I wanted dreadfully to get
To give to my Jemima.
[*Chorus*]
I see another snarl of men
A-digging graves, they told me,
So 'tarnal long, so 'tarnal deep,
They 'tended they should hold me.
[*Chorus*]
It scared me so, I hooked it off,
Nor stopped, as I remember,
Nor turned about till I got home,
Locked up in mother's chamber.
[*Chorus*]

title: Home on the Range
lyrics: Oh, give me a home where the buffalo roam,
Where the deer and the antelope play,
Where seldom is heard a discouraging word
And the skies are not cloudy all day.
Home, home on the range,
Where the deer and the antelope play;
Where seldom is heard a discouraging word
And the skies are not cloudy all day.
Where the air is so pure, the zephyrs so free,
The breezes so balmy and light,
That I would not exchange my home on the range
For all of the cities so bright.
The red man was pressed from this part of the West,
He's likely no more to return
To the banks of Red River where seldom if ever
Their flickering camp-fires burn.
How often at night when the heavens are bright
With the light from the glittering stars,
Have I stood here amazed and asked as I gazed
If their glory exceeds that of ours.
Oh, I love these wild flowers in this dear land of ours,
The curlew I love to hear scream,
And I love the white rocks and the antelope flocks
That graze on the mountain-tops green.
Oh, give me a land where the bright diamond sand
Flows leisurely down the stream;
Where the graceful white swan goes gliding along
Like a maid in a heavenly dream.
Then I would not exchange my home on the range,
Where the deer and the antelope play;
Where seldom is heard a discouraging word
And the skies are not cloudy all day.
Home, home on the range,
Where the deer and the antelope play;
Where seldom is heard a discouraging word
And the skies are not cloudy all day.

title: Green Grass Grows All Around
lyrics: All in a wood there grew a fine tree,
The finest tree that ever you did see,
And the green grass grew around, around, around,
And the green grass grew around.
And on this tree there grew a fine bough,
The finest bough that ever you did see,
And the bough on the tree, and the tree in the wood,
And the green leaves flourished thereon, thereon, thereon,
And the green leaves flourished thereon.
And on this bough there grew a fine twig,
The finest twig that ever you did see,
And the twig on the bough, and the bough on the tree, and the tree in the wood,
And the green leaves flourished thereon, etc.
And on this twig there stood a fine nest,
The finest nest that ever you did see,
And the nest on the twig, and the twig on the bough, etc.
And in this nest there sat a fine bird,
The finest bird, etc.
And on this bird there grew a fine feather,
The finest feather, etc.
And of this feather was made a fine bed,
The finest bed, etc.
And on this bed was laid a fine mother,
The finest mother, etc.
In the arms of this mother was laid a fine babe,
The finest babe, etc.
And the babe he grew up and became a fine boy,
The finest boy, etc.
And boy put an acorn all into the earth,
The finest acorn, etc.
And out of this acorn there grew a fine tree,
The finest tree, etc.
lyricsTitle: 「XXII. THE TREE IN THE WOOD」— A Book of Nursery Songs and Rhymes, ed. S. Baring-Gould, London: Methuen & Co., 1895（英文 Wikisource 所载、Wikipedia 条目链接的公版原文；为早期累积歌变体，非现代通行版本）
lyricsNote: 重要版本差异说明：Wikipedia 条目 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/And_the_Green_Grass_Grew_All_Around （亦名 The Green Grass Grew All Around／And the Green Grass Grows All Around）本身不印任何歌词，仅在 References 处以「English Wikisource has original text related to this article」链接到 https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Green_Grass_Grew_All_Around ；该 URL 实际重定向至 https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/A_Book_of_Nursery_Songs_and_Rhymes/The_Tree_in_the_Wood ，即 S. H. Mason 1877 年《Nursery Rhymes and Country Songs》，可能更古老；另有来源把 1912 年版本归为 William Jerome（词）与 Harry Von Tilzer（曲）（该年活页谱封面见条目图）；与爱尔兰民歌「The Rattlin' Bog」相似，各国异文众多。为遵守『不凭记忆补写』，未写出 Wikipedia 未印出的现代通行歌词。

title: Hush, Little Baby
lyrics: Hush, little baby, don't say a word,
Mama's gonna buy you a mockingbird.
If that mockingbird don't sing,
Mama's gonna buy you a diamond ring.
If that diamond ring turns brass,
Mama's gonna buy you a looking glass.
If that looking glass gets broke,
Mama's gonna buy you a billy-goat.
If that billy-goat don't pull,
Mama's gonna buy you a cart and bull.
If that cart and bull turn over,
Mama's gonna buy you a dog named Rover.
If that dog named Rover don't bark,
Mama's gonna buy you a horse and cart.
If that horse and cart fall down,
You'll still be the sweetest baby in town.
lyricsTitle: Wikipedia「Lyrics」节「The most common version of the lyrics are」下的最通行版本（8 组押韵对句）
lyricsNote: Wikipedia 以「The most common version of the lyrics are:」明确标出 8 组对句共 16 行，已逐行照录并保留原标点（行末为逗号或句号）。页面另说明结构简单、可按同一模式即兴增补对句，故异文极多；并引 1989 年 Target 广告「Amase」的改词变体「Hush, Apple Dumpling, don't say a word, / Cousin's gonna buy you a Mockingbird.」等，未计入 lyrics。历史与版本出处：作者与起源年代不详，一般认作美国南方传统摇篮曲，Roud Folk Song Index No. 470；Cecil Sharp 1918 年在弗吉尼亚州 Franklin County、Endicott 采记一版（VWML CJS2/10/4501），另在北卡 Micaville 记下 Julie Boone 唱的完整版（CJS2/9/3315、CJS2/10/4775）；James Madison Carpenter 约 1929–35 年在北卡 Durham 录有蜡筒（VWML SN18174）；Alan Lomax 1930–40 年代录有多种异文（含 Texas Gladden、Jean Ritchie 1949 年家族传本）；Wikipedia 认为今通行版本很可能源自 Jean Ritchie 的肯塔基家族版本，并经其影响 The Weavers、Joan Baez 等。
sourceTitle: Hush, Little Baby — Wikipedia，「Lyrics」节「The most common version of the lyrics are」
extraNotes: 公版依据：传统口头民歌，无署名作者，最早书面／录音记录自 1918 年起，相关采录本与 Roud 470 均为民俗采集材料。Wikipedia 另列 Inez & Charlie Foxx「Mockingbird」、Bo Diddley、Eminem「Mockingbird」等后世流行改编（有版权），与本条所录传统歌词无关。

title: All the Pretty Little Horses
lyrics: Hush a bye, don’t you cry,
Go to sleep, little baby.
And when you wake,
You shall have a cake,
and all the pretty little ponies.
Paint and bay,
sorrel and gray,
All the pretty little ponies.
So hush-a-by, Don't you cry,
Go to sleep, little baby.
lyricsTitle: Wikipedia「Lyrics § Dorothy Scarborough, 1925」小节所录版本（Dorothy Scarborough, On the Trail of Negro Folk-Songs, 1925）
lyricsNote: Wikipedia「Lyrics」节并列给出三种文本：①「Dorothy Scarborough, 1925」（上列 lyrics 逐行照录，保留原标点，含首行弯引号 don’t 与末段直引号 Don't 之差异）；②「Additional verse (included in some versions)」的「Way down yonder / In the meadow / Poor little baby crying momma / Birds and the butterflies / Flutter 'round his eyes / Poor little baby crying momma」及另一异文；③「Popular version」以音节连字符记录花腔唱法（如「Hush you bye, Don't you cry」「Go to sleep-y, my little ba - by.」「Blacks and bays, Dap-ples and grays, / Coach and six-a lit-tle hor-ses.」），并非干净刊本歌词。本题取有精确公版扫描出处的 1925 年 Scarborough 本作为可复核文本，未把「Popular version」的连字符文本校订为『通行歌词』，以免凭推测改写。版本出处：该曲亦名「Hush-a-bye」，美国传统摇篮曲，通行看法为非裔美国人起源；最早刊本为 Maud McKnight Lindsay 1903 年 10 月《Kindergarten Review》第 14 卷第 2 期第 106 页短篇「A White Dove」，其中注释为「an old lullaby」的 5 行作「All the pretty little horses, / White and gray and black and bay; / All the pretty little horses, / You shall see some day, some day— / All the pretty little horses.」；Dorothy Scarborough 1925 年《On the Trail of Negro Folk-Songs》（Harvard University Press, pp.144–149）记其为南方广为流传、异文极多的一首；John & Alan Lomax 1934 年《American Ballads and Folk Songs》(Macmillan, pp.304–305) 收同名版本，结尾含 po' lil lambie 与 Mammy 呼告的较灰暗异文。
sourceTitle: All the Pretty Little Horses — Wikipedia，「Lyrics § Dorothy Scarborough, 1925」；原刊扫描见 Internet Archive
extraNotes: 精确公版扫描 URL：https://archive.org/details/ontrailofnegrofo00scar/page/144 （Scarborough 1925, Lullabies 章）、https://archive.org/details/kindergartenrev00unkngoog/page/106 （Lindsay 1903「A White Dove」）、https://archive.org/details/americanballadsf0000john_m8i9/page/304 （Lomax 1934）。公版依据：传统摇篮曲，无署名作者，最早刊本 1903 年，上述引证书均出版于 1934 年以前。Angela Davis 1971 年曾据此讨论奴隶制下黑人母亲的处境（Wikipedia 引述），属后世评论。

title: Rock-a-bye Baby
lyrics: Rock a bye baby on the tree top,
When the wind blows the cradle will rock,
When the bough breaks the cradle will fall,
And down will come baby, cradle and all.
lyricsTitle: Wikipedia「Words」节所引 National Literacy Trust 的现代版本（One modern example, quoted by the National Literacy Trust）
lyricsNote: 已逐行照录 Wikipedia 引言块 4 行并保留原标点；Wikipedia 明确说明该童谣有多种版本，此处只是「One modern example」。版本出处与差异：Roud Folk Song Index No. 2768；最早被认为约 1765 年刊于伦敦《Mother Goose's Melody》（可能由 John Newbery 出版），1785 年波士顿重印；初版已无存本，1791 年版（W. F. Prideaux 1904 年影印本，Francis Power 出版）首句作「Hush-a-by baby」，童谣后附按语「This may serve as a warning to the proud and ambitious, who climb so high that they generally fall at last.」。James Orchard Halliwell《The Nursery Rhymes of England》(1842, p.124) 记早期《Gammer Gurton's Garland》(1784) 第三行作「When the wind ceases the cradle will fall」，并录第二行「When the bough bends」、第四行「Down will come baby, bough, cradle and all」。曲调方面 Iona & Peter Opie《The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes》(1997 年第 2 版 p.70) 记常用调为 Henry Purcell 1686 年《Lillibullero》的变体。Wikipedia 另列 1876 年 Clara L. Mateaux《Through Picture Land》、1881 年《St Nicholas Magazine》(M. E. Wilkins)、1885 年《Franklin Square Song Collection》(Robert Jones Burdette「American Cradle Song」) 等后世扩写本，以及 1918 年音乐剧《Sinbad》的「Rock-a-Bye Your Baby with a Dixie Melody」，均非本条 lyrics。
sourceTitle: Rock-a-bye Baby — Wikipedia，「Words」节（National Literacy Trust 引文）
extraNotes: 公版依据：作者不详，约 1765 年首见于《Mother Goose's Melody》，属 18 世纪传统童谣，Roud 2768。起源诸说（埃及 Horus、法语 He bas! là le loup!、五月花号殖民者、讽刺詹姆斯二世王室、德比郡 Betty Kenny 树屋传说等）Wikipedia 均列为未经证实的推测，本条不采信。

title: Brahms' Lullaby
lyrics: Guten Abend, gut' Nacht,
mit Rosen bedacht,
mit Näglein besteckt,
schlupf' unter die Deck':
Morgen früh, wenn Gott will,
wirst du wieder geweckt.
Guten Abend, gut' Nacht,
von Englein bewacht,
die zeigen im Traum
dir Christkindleins Baum:
schlaf nun selig und süß,
schau im Traum 's Paradies.
lyricsTitle: Wiegenlied (Lullaby / Cradle Song), Op. 49 No. 4 — 德文原词两段：第 1 段为 1868 年初版（取自《Des Knaben Wunderhorn》），第 2 段为后加的 Georg Scherer 1849 年诗
lyricsNote: 必须区分「原曲歌词」与「后世英文填词」：上列 lyrics 为 Wikipedia「Song § Lyrics」逐行照录的德文原词，共两段，标点原样保留（第 1 段末「wirst du wieder geweckt.」，第 2 段末「schau im Traum 's Paradies.」）。原曲歌词来源：第 1 段取自 Achim von Arnim 与 Clemens Brentano 编《Des Knaben Wunderhorn》之「Kinderlieder: Anhang zum Wunderhorn」(1808, Bd. III)，Wikipedia 标注为「First edition (1868)」；初版仅有一段。第 2 段是 Brahms 后来取自 Georg Scherer 1849 年诗补入（Wikipedia 标为「Georg Scherer (1849)」，并标注具体补入年份待考）。后世英文文本均非原曲歌词：① Wikipedia 页面给出的「Good evening, good night, / With roses covered, ...」是页面的散文式英译（Translation），非可演唱歌词；② Wikipedia 注释记 Natalia Macfarren 的英译「Brahms's Lullaby」（即通行「Lullaby and goodnight, with roses bedight...」一路文本）为 English version；③ 注释另记 William Engvick 所作英文歌词「Close Your Eyes」（Rosemary Clooney 1953 年、Frank Sinatra 1944 年 V-Disc 录音所用）为 20 世纪后世填词、有版权。本条 lyrics 只收德文原词。
sourceTitle: Wiegenlied (Brahms) — Wikipedia，「Song § Lyrics」德文原词两段（含页面英译与版本注释）
extraNotes: 曲目事实：Johannes Brahms《5 Lieder für eine Singstimme und Klavier》Op. 49 之第 4 首「Wiegenlied」，1868 年 11 月由 Simrock 出版，1869-12-22 在维也纳由 Luise Dustmann 演唱、Clara Schumann 伴奏首演；献给 Bertha Faber（次子出生），旋律部分受 Alexander Baumann 1840 年代二重唱「S'Is Anderscht」影响。公版依据：Brahms 1897 年逝世，1868 年出版物及《Des Knaben Wunderhorn》(1808)、Scherer(1849) 文本均在世界范围内进入公有领域；Wikipedia 外链指向 IMSLP 的「J. Brahms: 5 Songs, Op. 49」公版乐谱页。注意：Natalia Macfarren 英译本、William Engvick「Close Your Eyes」及各类 20 世纪改编可能有独立版权，publicDomain=true 仅指本条所录德文原词与原曲。

title: Golden Slumbers
lyrics: Golden slumbers kiss your eyes,
Smiles awake you when you rise.
Sleep, pretty wantons; do not cry,
And I will sing a lullaby:
Rock them, rock them, lullaby.
Care is heavy, therefore sleep you;
You are care, and care must keep you;
Sleep, pretty wantons; do not cry,
And I will sing a lullaby:
Rock them, rock them, lullaby
lyricsTitle: Thomas Dekker「Cradle Song」全诗两段 — 首刊于 1603 年剧作《Patient Grissel》（Wikipedia「Golden Slumbers」条目 Background 节所录）
lyricsNote: 必须区分「原曲歌词」与「后世英文填词／改编」：上列 lyrics 是 17 世纪原诗全文，Wikipedia 以「Cradle Song」标注并逐行照录；标点原样保留——第 1 段末「Rock them, rock them, lullaby.」有句号，第 2 段末「Rock them, rock them, lullaby」无句号，其余逗号、分号、冒号照录。原曲出处：Wikipedia 记「Golden Slumbers」基于剧作家 Thomas Dekker 的摇篮曲诗「Cradle Song」，1603 年首刊于剧作《Patient Grissel》（Sources 列 Dekker, Chettle, Haughton, 1603, The Pleasant Comodie of Patient Grissill）；1885 年《St Nicholas Songs》(p.177) 曾由 W. J. Henderson 谱曲、题作「Golden Slumbers Kiss Your Eyes」，后又有 Peter Warlock、Charles Villiers Stanford 与 Alfredo Casella 谱曲。后世改编（非原曲歌词）：Paul McCartney 在父亲利物浦家中看到继妹 Ruth 留在钢琴上的「Cradle Song」活页谱，因不识谱而另作新曲，仅取原诗第 1 段、略改数字，并加上一句反复的自创歌词；1969 年 The Beatles《Abbey Road》中的「Golden Slumbers」未给 Dekker 署名。McCartney 版旋律与新增歌词属 20 世纪有版权作品，绝不混入上列 lyrics。
sourceTitle: Golden Slumbers — Wikipedia，「Background」节所录 Thomas Dekker 1603 年「Cradle Song」全诗
extraNotes: 公版依据：Thomas Dekker 约 1572–1632，诗作 1603 年发表，作者逝世逾 400 年，原诗与原剧早已进入公有领域；publicDomain=true 仅指上列 1603 年原诗。Wikipedia Sources 另列 Lewisohn 1988、MacDonald 2005、Miles 1997、Sheff 2000 等关于 Beatles 版本的研究著作（有版权）。

title: All Through the Night
lyrics: Sleep my child and peace attend thee,
All through the night
Guardian angels God will send thee,
All through the night
Soft the drowsy hours are creeping
Hill and vale in slumber sleeping,
I my loving vigil keeping
All through the night.
While the moon her watch is keeping
All through the night
While the weary world is sleeping
All through the night
O'er thy spirit gently stealing
Visions of delight revealing
Breathes a pure and holy feeling
All through the night.
lyricsTitle: Sir Harold Boulton 1884 年填配的同曲调可唱英文歌词「Sleep my child and peace attend thee ... All through the night.」（Wikipedia「Ar Hyd y Nos」Lyrics 节）
lyricsNote: 必须区分「原曲歌词」与「后世英文填词」：本条 lyrics 是 1884 年 Sir Harold Boulton 为威尔士传统旋律新填的英文可唱歌词（Wikipedia 原文：「Singable English lyrics to the same tune were written by Sir Harold Boulton in 1884」），并非威尔士原词的翻译，已逐行照录并保留原标点（多数「All through the night」行无句末标点，每段末行有句号）。威尔士原曲歌词（原曲歌词）为 John Ceiriog Hughes（1832–1887）所作，Wikipedia「Lyrics」节以「Welsh」标出，首段逐行作：Holl amrantau'r sêr ddywedant / Ar hyd y nos / 「Dyma'r ffordd i fro gogoniant,」 / Ar hyd y nos. / Golau arall yw tywyllwch / I arddangos gwir brydferthwch / Teulu'r nefoedd mewn tawelwch / Ar hyd y nos. / Hyd y nos.（页面另附既非逐字、也非可唱的英文 Translation）。版本出处：曲调最早见于 Edward Jones（Bardd y Brenin）《Musical and Poetical Relics of the Welsh Bards》(1784)；Wikipedia 记最早英文版本之一为 Thomas Oliphant 1862 年据 John Jones (Talhaiarn) 另一套威尔士词所译（见 Welsh Melodies, With Welsh And English Poetry）；通行英文可唱词即 Boulton 1884 年本。Wikipedia 另列多种异文（第 2 段作「Angels watching ever round thee ...」、A. G. Prys-Jones 较贴近原意的押韵本「Ev'ry star in heaven is singing ...」、night song 文本「Deep the silence 'round us spreading ...」），均未混入 lyrics。
sourceTitle: Ar Hyd y Nos — Wikipedia，「Lyrics」节（Welsh 原词、Translation、Sir Harold Boulton 1884 英文可唱词及 Variations）
extraNotes: 相关精确 URL：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ar_Hyd_y_Nos ；Wikipedia 注明英文 Wikisource 收有「Ar Hyd y Nos」原文（https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Ar_Hyd_y_Nos ）、威尔士语 Wikisource 亦收「Ar hyd y nos」；IMSLP 收 Ar Hyd y Nos 乐谱；https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Through_the_Night_(Welsh_song) 不存在（返回「Wikipedia does not have an article with this exact name」）。同旋律另配 Reginald Heber 1821「God That Madest Earth and Heaven」、Fred Pratt Green 1970「For the Fruits of His Creation」、Jaroslav Vajda 1983「Go My Children with My Blessing」等圣诗（后两者文本有版权，Wikipedia 引 Hymnal「Praise for the Lord」#919 注明 words copyright 1970 by Hope Publishing Co.）。公版依据：1784 年曲调、Ceiriog Hughes（卒 1887）威尔士词、Boulton（1859–1935）1884 年英文词均进入公有领域；publicDomain=true 仅指本条所录 Boulton 词与传统旋律。

title: Lavender's Blue
lyrics: Lavender's blue, dilly dilly, lavender's green,
When I am king, dilly dilly, you shall be queen:
Who told you so, dilly dilly, who told you so?
'Twas mine own heart, dilly dilly, that told me so.
Call up your men, dilly dilly, set them to work,
Some with a rake, dilly dilly, some with a fork;
Some to make hay, dilly dilly, some to thresh corn,
Whilst you and I, dilly dilly, keep ourselves warm.
If you should die, dilly dilly, as it may hap,
You shall be buried, dilly dilly, under the tap;
Who told you so, dilly dilly, pray tell me why?
That you might drink, dilly dilly, when you are dry.
lyricsTitle: Wikipedia「Lyrics」节所录 James Orchard Halliwell 1849 年的典型版本（A typical version, described by James Halliwell in 1849）
lyricsNote: 已逐行照录 Wikipedia 明确标出的 3 段共 12 行并保留原标点（含冒号、分号、'Twas 的省字符）。Wikipedia 说明全曲可多至 30 段、每段又有众多异文，此处仅为 Halliwell 1849 年的「typical version」。版本出处：该曲为 17 世纪英格兰民歌／童谣，Roud Folk Song Index No. 3483；最早存世版本为 1672–1679 年间英格兰印行的 broadside「Diddle Diddle, or The Kind Country Lovers」（题注「to the tune of Lavender Green」，内容较俚俗；Wikipedia 引其十段中的第 1 段「Lavender's green, diddle, diddle, / Lavender's blue / You must love me, diddle, diddle, / cause I love you, / I heard one say, diddle, diddle, / since I came hither, / That you and I, diddle, diddle, / must lie together.」）；英文 Wikisource 收该 broadside 原题「Diddle, Diddle: Or, The Kind Country Lovers」。作为儿童歌曲成型于 1805 年《Songs for the Nursery》：「Lavender blue and Rosemary green, / When I am king you shall be queen; / Call up my maids at four o'clock, / Some to the wheel and some to the rock; / Some to make hay and some to shear corn, / And you and I will keep the bed warm.」。Halliwell 引文出自《Popular Rhymes and Nursery Tales》(London: John Russell Smith, 1849, pp.237–238)；Opie 夫妇《The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes》(1951, pp.265–7) 亦录；Walter Crane 编《The Baby's Opera》(1877, p.17) 收带插图的歌词与谱。
sourceTitle: Lavender's Blue — Wikipedia，「Lyrics」节（Halliwell 1849 典型版本）
extraNotes: 版权提示：1948 年迪士尼电影《So Dear to My Heart》中 Burl Ives 演唱的「Lavender Blue (Dilly Dilly)」由 Eliot Daniel（曲）与 Larry Morey（词）署名，获 1949 年奥斯卡最佳原创歌曲提名，属有版权的后世改编，Wikipedia 明确单列，绝不混入上列传统歌词。公版依据：17 世纪 broadside（1672–1679）、1805 年《Songs for the Nursery》、1849 年 Halliwell 本均为公有领域。Wikipedia 并提及该曲与 Twelfth Night 选「king and queen」习俗的关联。

title: Simple Gifts
lyrics: 'Tis the gift to be simple, 'tis the gift to be free
'Tis the gift to come down where we ought to be,
And when we find ourselves in the place just right,
'Twill be in the valley of love and delight.
When true simplicity is gained,
To bow and to bend we shan’t be ashamed,
To turn, turn will be our delight,
Till by turning, turning we come 'round right.
lyricsTitle: Simple Gifts（1848 年 Joseph Brackett 原始一节，Copland 所用歌词）
lyricsNote: 逐行照录英文维基百科 Simple Gifts 条目 Lyrics 节所引原始一节，该处引文标注 Anderson, John M.,「Force and Form: The Shaker Intuition of Simplicity」, The Journal of Religion 30(4), 1950, pp.256–260, doi:10.1086/484020。条目另列三段后世非震教徒增补歌词与多个现代改编版本，均非 1848 年原文，未一并录入、未作扩写。词曲一般归于缅因州 Alfred 震教徒村长老 Joseph Brackett（1797–1882），作于 1848 年；条目称最早记载为 1848 年 10 月新格洛斯特震教徒家族音乐会广告。1848 年作品，公有领域。

title: Frog Went A-Courting（其他传统版本）
lyrics: A frog he would a-wooing go,
Heigho, says Rowley,
Whether his mother would let him or no.
With a rowley powley, gammon and spinach,
Heigho, says Anthony Rowley!
So off he set with his opera hat,
Heigho, says Rowley,
And on the road he met with a rat.
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mr. Rat, will you go with me,
Heigho, says Rowley,
Kind Mistress Mousey for to see?'
With a rowley powley, etc.
And when they came to Mousey's hall,
Heigho, says Rowley,
They gave a loud knock, and they gave a loud call.
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mistress Mouse, are you within?'
Heigho, says Rowley.
'Oh yes, kind sirs, I'm sitting to spin.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mistress Mouse, will you give us some beer?
Heigho, says Rowley,
For Froggy and I are fond of good cheer.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Pray, Mr. Frog, will you give us a song?
Heigho, says Rowley,
But let it be something that's not very long.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Indeed, Mistress Mouse,' replied Mr. Frog,
Heigho, says Rowley,
'A cold has made me as hoarse as a dog.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
'Since you have caught cold, Mr. Frog,' Mousey said,
Heigho, says Rowley,
'I'll sing you a song that I have just made.'
With a rowley powley, etc.
But while they were all a merry-making,
Heigho, says Rowley,
A cat and her kittens came tumbling in.
With a rowley powley, etc.
The cat she seized the rat by the crown;
Heigho, says Rowley,
The kittens they pulled the little mouse down.
With a rowley powley, etc.
This put Mr. Frog in a terrible fright;
Heigho, says Rowley,
He took up his hat, and wished them goodnight.
With a rowley powley, etc.
But as Froggy was crossing over a brook,
Heigho, says Rowley,
A lily-white duck came and gobbled him up,
With a rowley powley, etc.
So there was an end of one, two, and three,
Heigho, says Rowley,
The rat, and the mouse, and the little froggee,
With a rowley powley, gammon and spinach,
Heigho, says Anthony Rowley!

title: Arroz con leche
lyrics: Arroz con leche me quiero casar
con una señorita de la capital,
que sepa coser,
que sepa contar,
que sepa abrir la puerta
para ir a jugar.
Yo soy la viudita, del barrio del rey,
Me quiero casar y no encuentro con quien:
con este, sí, con este, no;
contigo, mi vida, me casar yo.
